title.narrative: Provision of integrated lifesaving assistance in four drought affected districts of Manica and Sofala provinces

description.narrative: The climate shocks disproportionately affect vulnerable households including rural, rainfed agricultural communities. Increased drought frequency in Mozambique continues to drive humanitarian crises as communities experience reduced food production, income loss, and limited access to essential services. The 2023 El Niño event worsened Mozambique’s food insecurity. Disrupted rainfall and temperature patterns heavily impacted agriculture, with Ministry of Agriculture assessments revealing a 19% reduction in crop yields across 591,541 hectares or a loss of 720,000 tons of cereals.In priority districts of Guro, Macossa, Tambara and Maringue, over 189,000 people are affected, including ~72,000 classified as IPC Phase 4 (Emergency), requiring urgent assistance. Poor harvests have led to displacements and coping strategies including migration to areas with better agricultural conditions and services. The 2024/2025 forecast anticipates normal to above-normal rainfall. Rain could improve agricultural prospects, but increases risks of flooding in river basins. The likelihood of frequent storms underscores the urgent need for climate resilience. Addressing immediate humanitarian needs while fostering climate adaptation will reduce vulnerability in the targeted communities.UNICEF will address needs in WASH, Nutrition and Child Protection with integrated social behaviour change actions. Mitigation measures against gender-based violence, sexual exploitation and abuse, negative coping strategies and harmful practices will be adopted across sectors. Overall, UNICEF intend to reach a total of 63,763 people which 64% are children as described below.WASH will address the needs of at least 25,000 people focusing on restoring access to water, distribution of essential WASH supplies; rehabilitation of school and health care facility WASH systems, and rehab/construction of sanitation facilities. Under the climate envelope, climate resilient water supply services will be established, introducing an additional climate risk, groundwater assessment and an estimate of unmet and projected needs. These systems will be complemented by Rainwater Harvesting Systems as an alternative water source in 2 schools for further drought risk mitigation. The project will strengthen water safety and adaptation planning, institutionalize drought preparedness and build back better learnings. Overall, 6,500 people will benefit from climate resilient water supply, including 300 students from additional water sources in schools. Indirect beneficiaries from improved water safety and district-level adaptation planning are 116,000.Nutrition and SBC will provide lifesaving screening and treatment for severe acute malnutrition for children under 5 years, and provide gender-responsive feeding counselling and support to caregivers. Activities include delivery of lifesaving health and nutrition supplies, case identification through screenings, and outreach with integrated mobile brigades, vitamin A supplementation, and training on acute malnutrition management. Mass media, interpersonal communication, and community platforms will be used to support the adoption of life-saving practices reaching approximately 40,000 people. Interventions will use behavioral evidence to address bottlenecks towards the adoption of nutrition and WASH-related practices.Child Protection services aim to reach 6,941 children with mental health and psychosocial support activities, counselling, identification and referral of vulnerable children to basic social services and protection through case management, identification of unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), support for temporary alternative care as needed, prevention and response to violence against children and gender-based violence through social media and mass media, centers for assistance to survivors of violence, prevention and response to sexual exploitation and abuse, and dissemination of information on channels to report allegations.
